name: Fen Ellis
home: the western blocks near Ferry Street Rooms
life: Fen drew birds as a child because the family moved too often to keep pets. He signed his first paid shopfront with a tiny gull where only someone opening the shutter could see it. Friday often includes a stop at the crossing outside Verve Nail Studio, where Fen notices whose chair is empty and who has stayed talking after an appointment.
voice: The chalk gull underneath is mine. I used to draw birds under things at friends' houses. This is the first time one of them has flown back.
appearance: Fen is easy to recognize by dark brown curls cut close behind the ears and a small notch in the left eyebrow. Usually dressed in an old plum windbreaker with a partly rubbed-away embroidered initial, Fen looks at people's hands before looking at what they carry when listening.
personality: Fen finds it easier to own up to a mistake than to accept praise. The worse the mistake, the more precise the account of exactly when it happened.
agenda: To find one of the other childhood gulls before an old house is sold.
family: Hollis Osei is Fen’s older relative by marriage. Fen remembers the birthdays. Hollis asks what the birthday guest would like this year. A present that was perfect at sixteen may be completely wrong at forty. They take the trouble of finding out. Asked about *A tenant who stays*, Hollis says, “I would share the big room for a season. Nobody asked because they thought an old person always wants silence.”
connections: Tamsin Leung. A chalk gull lets them test two very different ideas about who used to sit here. Also in the story is Owen Vale (childhood friend).

reactions.situation: Two families claim the kitchen chair
reactions.response: Fen asks each claimant what they remember about the seat before the marks are shown.

reactions.situation: A driver splashes a market worker and tries to laugh it off
reactions.response: Fen helps shift the damp stock and makes sure the worker gets to describe the loss without interruption.
